cross_cutting_findings.title: The CI security job's governing rationale is stale and self-sealing
cross_cutting_findings.evidence: .github/workflows/deploy.yml L52-56 and L80-84 assert 'This repository is PRIVATE' and that code scanning + secret scanning are 'confirmed UNAVAILABLE on this private repo without a paid GitHub plan', instructing 'do not re-investigate this as an open question; the answer is a paid-plan upgrade.' The repository is now public (verified via API: "private": false, "visibility": "public"). CodeQL code scanning and secret scanning are both free on public repositories. Issue #353 independently confirms secret scanning is already live — alert #1 fired when the repo went public on 2026-07-31.
cross_cutting_findings.impact: A comment telling future maintainers not to re-investigate is now actively wrong, and it guards the single largest gap in the security job. The job today runs Trivy only, with exit-code 0 (report-only) and no SARIF upload, so it produces no enforced findings whatsoever.
cross_cutting_findings.recommended_action: Re-enable CodeQL (init + analyze + upload-sarif) now that it is free, and correct the stale comments. Belongs to #290.

cross_cutting_findings.title: #290's 'what already exists' table no longer matches the workflow
cross_cutting_findings.evidence: Issue says the security job runs 'CodeQL init (javascript) + Trivy fs scan -> SARIF upload'. Actual active steps are checkout + Trivy only; every codeql reference in the file is inside a comment block (L53-56, L64-65). Issue says 'Node is pinned to 20'; the workflow sets NODE_VERSION: '22' (L17). Issue asks to confirm whether 'develop' is still used; `git ls-remote --heads origin` returns no refs/heads/develop, so it is dead and should be dropped from the push trigger.
cross_cutting_findings.impact: Three of the issue's stated premises are false, so an implementer working from the issue body alone would produce wrong changes.
cross_cutting_findings.recommended_action: Rescope #290 against the current workflow before implementing.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Two milestone issues are blocked independently of Codex
cross_cutting_findings.evidence: #226 requires enumerating anon-key-reachable objects against a live database. #225 requires RLS_TEST_* credentials and a designated non-production Supabase project. Neither is satisfiable from repository evidence, and the Supabase MCP server cannot be approved in a non-interactive session.
cross_cutting_findings.impact: These two remain blocked even after Codex is restored.

issues.title: Run RLS verification in CI so security regressions fail the build
issues.investigation: scripts/verify-rls-security.mjs exists (441 lines) and is the intended instrument. Wiring it into CI needs RLS_TEST_* secrets and an owner decision on which project it runs against — the issue itself requires that decision be recorded deliberately. Guardrail forbids running destructive verification against production.
issues.note: The workflow scaffolding could be written by Codex, but the issue cannot be closed until the project + credential decision is made by a human.

What is missing is any test guarding it: zero test files under src/data. This is a pure test-authoring issue against existing, correct behavior — low risk, high value.

issues.title: Remove or nonce the inline theme bootstrap script (CSP blocker)
issues.investigation: CONFIRMED LIVE. public/index.html L39-55 contains an inline <script> IIFE reading localStorage 'theme' and applying a class to documentElement for FOUC prevention before first paint. This is the concrete blocker to a CSP without unsafe-inline. It is independent of the collector work and can proceed in parallel with #221.
issues.sequencing: Do FIRST in the CSP cluster alongside #221 — it unblocks #223 and #224.
issues.hazard: Removing it naively reintroduces a flash of unstyled content; a nonce or hash approach preserves the pre-paint behavior.
